All Pair Shortest Path: Recursive Algorithm
Algorithm 1 APSP-Recursive
Input: A directed graph G = (V, E)
Output: Shortest distance between all pair of vertices
1: n ← |G.V| . Number of vertices in G
2: m ← |G.E| . Number of edges in G
3: Create a distance matrix D[1, 2, . . . , n][1, 2, . . . , n] of size n × n
4: for each vertex u ∈ G.V do
5: for each vertex v ∈ G.V do
6: D[u][v] ← APSP-Helper(n − 1, u, v) . Weight of a shortest path from vertex u
to vertex v that contains at most n − 1 edges
7: return D

Algorithm 2 APSP-Helper(r, u, v)
1: if r = 0 then
2: if u = v then
3: return 0 . Weight of a shortest path from vertex u to vertex v that contains
at most 0 edge is 0 because vertex u and vertex v are the same
4: else
5: return ∞ . Weight of a shortest path from vertex u to vertex v that contains
at most 0 edge is ∞ because vertex u and vertex v are different
6: else
7: minDistance ← ∞
8: for each vertex k ∈ G.V do
9: dist ← APSP-Helper(r − 1, u, k) + w(k, v)
10: if dist < minDistance then
11: minDistance ← dist
12: return minDistance
